GOVERNMENT BILL 
The Carriage by Air (Amendment) Bill, 2008 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION (SHRI PRAFUL PATEL): 
Sir, I beg to move: 
That the Bill further to amend the Carriage by Air Act, 1972, as passed by  
Lok Sabha, be taken into consideration. 

 316
 Sir, I place before this august House for it s consideration and passing the Carriage by Air 
(Amendment) Bill, 2008, which has been passed by the Lok Sabha on 30th April 2008. 
Sir, as you are all aware, during the last de cade, there have been significant developments 
in the civil aviation sector bringing India to the co re of the international civil aviation scenario. We 
have now, in fact, become a trendsetter due to our size and impressive growth rates. To further 
place India in the ranks of global leaders, I prop ose this legislation which will facilitate higher 
compensation and prevent Indian passengers from discrimination. 
On our proposal for amendment of the Act, I would like to mention that there is an 
international legal regime governing the liability of air carriers for injury or death of passengers, 
for destruction or loss of or damage to bagg age or cargo, and losses caused by delay in 
international carriage of passenge rs, baggage and cargo. This regi me is set out in a number of 
international instruments. 
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, legislative business is going on, I request you to 
kindly maintain decorum. 
SHRI PRAFUL PATEL: However, India has so fa r ratified only two instruments, namely, the 
Warsaw Convention, 1929, and the Warsaw Conv ention as amended by The Hague Protocol, 
1955 and the same has been given effect to by the Carriage by Air Act, 1972. India has not yet 
acceded to the Montreal Convention, 1999. However,  it has become necessary now for India to 
accede to this Convention to bring uniformity in th e applications of the liability regime ending the 
multiplicity of international instruments. We have  to bring India on a par with all international 
conventions. 
The various instruments adopted by the Internat ional Civil Aviation Organisation failed to 
receive the kind of universal acceptance as the present Warsaw Convention and the Hague 
Protocol had received. Consequently their coming into force was inordinately delayed due to 
which several States chose to go ahead with thei r unilateral decisions to increase the liability 
limits. This, therefore, resulted  in a situation where several different combinations of liability 
regimes came into existence defying the much desi red uniformity and unific ation of international 
law in this field. The ICAO then embarked upon  serious initiative for a socio-economic study of 
the levels of compensation and undertook the modernisation and conso lidation of the Warsaw 
System, which produced the text of the new Convention. 
Finally, the Montreal Convention, 1999 was adopted for the unification of certain rules for 
international carriage by air which aims to achi eve the dual purpose of modernising as well as 
consolidating the various instruments comprising the Warsaw System.  
Sir, when there is an injury or there is a loss of baggage or cargo, today, you get one  
kind of compensation in India, other kind of compensation in America, and some other kind of 

 317
compensation in Europe. Therefore, the Montreal Convention is to bring every country which is a 
signatory to the ICAO on a par with other conventions as far as compensation or liability is 
concerned. Therefore, we also as a member Stat e are now required to do it, because it would 
be discriminatory as long as we are not a si gnatory to it. Suppose our passenger is on an 
international aircraft, not of India. There would be two liability regimes for Indian passenger, 
because we have not ratified it. So, he would be eligible for ‘x’ compensation which would be, at 
the present moment, less than what his counterpa rt traveller on the same aircraft would be 
entitled to. Because the country of origin of that aircraft or the domicile of that passenger would 
be governed by the other regime. Therefore, we as a member nation to the ICAO are required to 
be acceding to this convention. Therefore, it wo uld require a change in the existing Act itself. 
That is what this legislation seeks to bring about. 
It has, of course, been vetted by the Standi ng Committee and has been passed by the Lok 
Sabha in April 2008. Therefore, I would request this  august House to take up this legislation and 
extend its full support. 
The question was proposed.
